subject.title: [Feature]: Recover the in-flight gateway run on CLI disconnect (reattach-first) instead of recook-first embedded fallback

question: After a bounded reattach and replay attempt cannot prove the original accepted run’s terminal outcome, should `openclaw agent` preserve the isolated embedded rerun by default, fail closed unless users opt in to rerun, or split that policy by delivery mode?
rationale: This determines a public CLI compatibility contract: automatic rerun favors result availability but risks duplicate side effects, while fail-closed recovery favors single execution but can withhold a result. Source-level correctness cannot select that tradeoff safely.

options.title: Preserve fallback by default
options.body: After bounded reattach/replay fails, retain the isolated fresh-session embedded fallback so existing CLI users still receive a result, while keeping the recovery-first path.

options.title: Fail closed by default
options.body: Return an ambiguous-outcome error unless the user explicitly opts in to a rerun that may duplicate side effects.

options.title: Split by mode
options.body: Use recovery-first fail-closed behavior for `--deliver` and preserve isolated fallback for interactive stdout runs.

recommendation.title: Preserve fallback by default
recommendation.body: After bounded reattach/replay fails, retain the isolated fresh-session embedded fallback so existing CLI users still receive a result, while keeping the recovery-first path.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue’s latest discussion directly requests this person’s decision on the compatibility default.
